findings.note: AnnotationLine.value was typed `unknown` and both builder and parser wrote null for the absent case, collapsing the store's two distinct states (value_json IS NULL vs value_json = 'null') into one. Fixed before merge across five sites by making absence an omitted key, and guarded by packages/cli/test/corpus-lines.test.ts.
Checked whether the pass-identity assertion could pass vacuously; it cannot -- its fixture guard expect(sourcePasses).toHaveLength(2) fails first if annotateTwice stops producing two passes.

The implementation escalated one inference for confirmation: scheme registration restores created_at verbatim rather than stamping this.now(). Confirmed correct, and forced rather than optional -- the round-trip test asserts byte-identical re-export and the scheme line carries created_at, so the import clock would fail an already-asserted contract. corpus.ts calls entry_types.registered_at the one column that cannot be restored; that is a limitation for types, not a precedent for schemes.

properties.stage: asc-6u5 -- asc export drops annotations and schemes

findings.note: Replacement enumerated the fields believed to carry labels -- properties, evidence_text, scheme SQL -- so any other string field would have survived redaction silently. Correct on today's data by accident of the data, not by construction. Replaced with a line-level deep walk; 2 of the 4 tests added for the new rule fail against the enumerated version.

A refactor narrowed the home-path residue scan from every corpus line to entry lines only, while its doc comment asserted behaviour was unchanged. Measured 1806 -> 1800. Independent scan by line kind: type 5, entry 1800, scheme 1. The single lost scheme line is rule-denial -- the one line in the corpus whose SQL carries real project labels. Fixed by splitting DisclosedVocabulary from IdentityVocabulary so the narrow function cannot return the field at all, and restoring the whole-stream scan; 2 new guards fail against the regressed version.
disclosingHasHomePath left orphaned by the fix above. Deleted.

properties.stage: asc-hqr -- The discriminators must distinguish without disclosing

evidence_text: asc-hqr code review across three implementation agents. Two silent-narrowing defects of the same shape: a rule stated over a subset while reading as if stated over the whole. Both would have produced a redacted-looking export that still disclosed, and neither was reachable by any test the narrowed version would have been written with.

findings.note: ARCHITECTURE.md:419 says the skill 'doubles as a recall surface, partially mitigating the pull-only recording risk'. The delivered skill implemented only the half that stops an analyst excluding a population they did not know existed -- run bare asc first. The half where the ANALYSIS ITSELF gets recorded was missing, which is the half that actually addresses pull-only recording. Added a closing section routing evidence_record vs decision by the types' own record_when contracts, requiring the measurement be copied verbatim rather than paraphrased, and asking for a back-tested-and-REJECTED rule to be recorded too.

Not a defect -- a false alarm I raised and then disproved, recorded because the disproof is the useful part. Removing the skill directory appeared to SKIP three tests rather than fail, which would have made the guard silently stop guarding. Re-measured without a grep filter: the suite reports 'Test Files 1 failed', the beforeAll raises ENOENT naming the path, and the process exits 1. My grep had matched the 'Tests' summary line and missed the failure line above it -- the same pattern-too-narrow mistake that lost the red test name for asc-9ac.

properties.stage: E10 -- analysis-method skill, /ascend-analyze, and asc install-skill

evidence_text: E10 review across three implementation agents. Every flag citation in the skill was checked against the real command surface and all held: --cluster ships no default --threshold on purpose (EV-21), --linkage defaults to average, --distinctive needs --by, kappa takes two --scheme or one --scheme with two --pass, MIN_N = 20 at packages/analysis/src/proportion.ts:50. The drift guard was mutation-tested rather than accepted: a bogus flag, a bogus command, and a missing skill directory each turn it red.

findings.note: entry_types_identity_is_immutable's RAISE text still says only status, description and record_when may change; prose_json and now guidance_json also may. Lives in migration 1's DDL, so fixing it needs a trigger rebuild in a new migration.

A new VERSION registered from a document that omits guidance starts with none; guidance is not carried forward from the previous version. Same existing semantics as description/record_when, but review_after dropping out of the brief on a shape bump is more surprising.

The advisory reads the LATEST version's review_after even when --type-version targets an older one; the count spans every version. Deliberate (the intention belongs to the type), not tested for the --type-version case.
